title: Two rates over 25 years
label: Both yields fall over the 25 years.
The 10-year Treasury yield goes from about 8 percent in 1990 to about 2 percent in 2015.
The 3-month yield swings more, because it follows the rate set by the Federal Reserve.
For most of the chart the 10-year yield sits above the 3-month yield.

title: Last time, a puzzle: 2004 to 2006
label: The Fed started raising rates in 2004.
From June 2004 to June 2006 the 3-month yield rose steadily, from 1.3 to 4.9 percent.
The 10-year yield barely moved, staying between 4.0 and 5.1 percent.

title: Deep in the valley: 2008 to 2015
label: In response to the recession, the Federal Reserve kept short-term rates near zero.
The 3-month yield drops from 2.8 percent in January 2008 to 0.03 percent in December 2008,
and stays below 0.3 percent through March 2015.

title: Highest month: September 1990
label: The 10-year yield averaged 8.89 percent in September 1990, the highest month in the chart.

title: Lowest 10-year yield: July 2012
label: The 10-year yield averaged 1.53 percent in July 2012, the lowest month in the chart.
On July 25 it closed at 1.43 percent.
